report.summary: Chunk 2 of 2: defines imports_resolve, run_checks, with_markers, and unresolved_first_party_imports; includes docstrings and comments with claims about behaviour.
risks: unresolved_first_party_imports | medium | The function catches SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError but not other exceptions; if ast.parse raises something else, it propagates. | Confirm that ast.parse only raises those exceptions or add a broader catch.

imports_resolve | medium | Docstring says 'Checked for CREATED files too' but the function itself does not distinguish CREATED vs MODIFIED; it relies on attempt.is_python and calls unresolved_first_party_imports. The claim is uncheckable because the WriteAttempt type is not in this chunk. | Review WriteAttempt to see if CREATED files are handled differently.

run_checks | high | Docstring says 'FAIL-CLOSED' and catches Exception, but the except clause uses bare 'Exception' which is broad; BLE001 is noqa'd. This is a deliberate design choice but may mask unexpected errors. | Consider if more specific exceptions should be caught or if the noqa is justified.
with_markers | low | The docstring says 'Convenience only' but the function is a simple wrapper; no risk identified.

handoff.purpose: Defines unresolved_first_party_imports, imports_resolve, run_checks, and with_markers; implements import resolution checks.

symbols.name: unresolved_first_party_imports
symbols.note: Returns list of bad import strings; uses ast module to parse content, walks tree, checks module existence and exports.

symbols.name: imports_resolve
symbols.note: Calls unresolved_first_party_imports and formats error message; returns empty string if no issues.

symbols.name: BASELINE
symbols.note: Tuple of check functions: not_truncated, no_elision, parses, not_substituted, imports_resolve.

symbols.name: run_checks
symbols.note: Iterates over checks, catches exceptions, returns refusal or empty string.

symbols.name: with_markers
symbols.note: Returns new CheckPolicy with added elision markers.

claims.text: Conservative by construction, because a false refusal costs real work: * only first-party roots are judged; * a missing MODULE is reported, since that cannot be a re-export; * a missing NAME is reported only when the module has no star-import and no module-level ``__getattr__``.
claims.why: The code checks alias.name.split('.')[0] in roots, reports missing module, and checks opaque (star-import or __getattr__) before reporting missing name.

claims.text: Deduplicated but order-preserving: the same bad import repeated ten times is one problem, and the first occurrence is the one worth naming.
claims.why: Return uses list(dict.fromkeys(bad)) which preserves order and removes duplicates.

claims.text: Checked for CREATED files too -- a brand-new test module against an invented API is exactly the failure this catches, and it has no original to compare against.
claims.why: The function does not reference file status; relies on attempt object not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Cheapest first. Order is load-bearing in one direction only -- the refusal a caller sees should be the most specific one available, and 'does not parse' is more useful than '82% of definitions vanished' when both are true.
claims.why: The order of checks is defined but the relative cost or specificity of each check is not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: FAIL-CLOSED, and this is the part worth not losing: a check that raises is reported as a refusal naming the crash. The alternative -- letting the exception propagate, or catching it and continuing -- turns a broken guard into a silent permission, which is how a gate ends up passing a file that destroyed a module.
claims.why: The code catches Exception and returns a refusal string with the exception info, thus failing closed.

claims.text: A lane may pass ``extra`` to ADD checks. There is deliberately no argument for removing one from the baseline.
claims.why: Function signature includes extra: Iterable[Check] = () and iterates over (*BASELINE, *extra); no parameter to remove checks.

claims.text: ``policy`` with this lane's own elision markers. Convenience only.
claims.why: Function returns replace(policy, elision_markers=tuple(markers)), which is a convenience wrapper.

observations.what: unresolved_first_party_imports catches SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError but not other exceptions from ast.parse.
The docstring of imports_resolve claims to check CREATED files, but the function does not differentiate file status.
run_checks catches Exception broadly and noqa's BLE001 (blind except).
with_markers is a thin wrapper; no issues.
